label: prop:hadron-half-life
title: Hadron half-life from the $q$-deformed transition amplitude
html:
A nucleus displaced from the valley of stability (integer stability) undergoes beta decay. The substrate parameter q (substrate parameter) governs the half-life via the q-deformed transition amplitude.

Proposition. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the Descartes universe with substrate parameter q, and let \mathcal{N}(Z, N) (stable nucleus) be a nucleus with proton displacement \delta p = p - p_{\mathrm{stab}}(A) from the valley of stability. The beta-decay half-life is

  t_{1/2}(p, A)
  = 
  \frac{\ln 2}{\Gamma_\beta(p, A)},
  \qquad
  \Gamma_\beta(p, A)
  = 
  \frac{|\mathcal{W}(q)|^2 \cdot \mu_0}{2\pi^3}
   \cdot 
  [2]_q
   \cdot 
  |\mathcal{M}_q|^2
   \cdot 
  f(Q),

where \mathcal{W}(q) = \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5) in H_3(q) is the weak vertex form factor of the mediating torus knot T_{3,5} (beta decay as crossing change); [2]_q = q + q^{-1} is the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) fundamental dimension; |\mathcal{M}_q|^2 is the parent/daughter Markov-trace ratio (trace ratio observable); and f(Q) \propto Q^5 is the Sargent phase-space integral in the Q-value (transition energy). The decay rate depends only on q and the dimensional scale \mu_0 (building blocks).
